lockedMove.speaker: William Lane Craig
lockedMove.proposition: If infinite time and a one-to-one correspondence suffice to finish a reverse countdown, the counter should have finished at every earlier time, contradicting the claim that the counting continued eternally.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: sufficient condition for finishing the countdown then why didn't he finish his countdown yesterday or the day before that by then he'd already had an infinite amount of time to finish his countdown and so he should already be done in fact no matter how far you regresses the past at every point he should have already finished because he's had an infinite amount of time to finish the countdown but then it's not true that he has been counting

components.text: The decisive demand is whether an infinite past process can coherently complete at the present without already completing earlier.

response.rationale: The reply shifts from future counting to a reverse countdown and argues that the proposed sufficient conditions would apply at every earlier time.
